hook: The farm boy who put the world on wheels with the Model T and the assembly line.

pages.t: A farm boy who loved machines
pages.x: Henry Ford was born in 1863 on a farm in Dearborn, Michigan. He hated farm work but loved machines, and repaired his neighbours' watches. At 16 he walked to Detroit to become an apprentice machinist.

Working as an engineer for an electric company in Detroit, in 1896 he built his first car, the Quadricycle, in a shed behind his house. It was wider than the shed door, so he knocked down part of the wall to drive it out.
In 1908 he launched the Model T, a simple, tough car "for the great multitude". From 1914 it came only in black, because black paint dried fastest: "Any colour, so long as it is black."
In 1913, at his Highland Park factory, the cars moved past the workers on a conveyor, and each worker did one job. Building a Model T went from about 12 hours to about 90 minutes.
pages.fx: The price of a Model T fell from 850 to under 300 dollars, and mass production spread to almost every industry.

pages.x: In 1914 he doubled his workers' pay to five dollars a day, so that they would stay, and could afford to buy the cars they built.
By 1927 Ford had built more than 15 million Model Ts. For a time, about half of all the cars in America were Model Ts.
In the 1920s his newspaper spread hatred of Jews, in articles that Hitler admired. He also fought trade unions with spies and thugs, who in 1937 beat up union organisers outside his factory.
Ford put the world on wheels, and his assembly line became the way the modern world makes almost everything.
pts: Built the Model T, the car for everyone
